# Level commands

<!-- ANCHOR: commands -->

## `xrf-cli level info`

Command to print information about a compiled level

```txt
xrf-cli level info [OPTIONS] <--path <path>|--root <root>>
```

| Option                 | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `-p, --path <path>`    |          |         | Path to a compiled level directory, the one holding `level` and `level.geom`                                                                                 |
| `-r, --root <root>...` |          |         | Root holding an installation's levels. Repeat to layer roots, highest priority first                                                                         |
| `-l, --level <level>`  |          |         | Name of the level to read from the mounted roots, as `levels` knows it                                                                                       |
| `--source <source>`    |          | `auto`  | How a root is mounted, which for an installation is the default. Possible values: `auto`, `directory`, `volumes`, `installation`, `containing-installation`. |
| `-s, --silent`         |          |         | Turn off logging                                                                                                                                             |
| `-v, --verbose`        |          |         | Turn on verbose logging                                                                                                                                      |
| `--json`               |          |         | Write the run's JSON report to stdout, moving human output to stderr                                                                                         |
| `--report <PATH>`      |          |         | Write the run's JSON report to a file                                                                                                                        |

## `xrf-cli level verify`

Command to verify a compiled level's geometry can be drawn the way the renderer addresses it

```txt
xrf-cli level verify [OPTIONS] <--path <path>|--root <root>>
```

| Option                 | Required | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------- | -------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `-p, --path <path>`    |          |         | Path to a compiled level directory, the one holding `level` and `level.geom`                                                                                 |
| `-r, --root <root>...` |          |         | Root holding an installation's levels. Repeat to layer roots, highest priority first                                                                         |
| `-l, --level <level>`  |          |         | Name of the level to read from the mounted roots, as `levels` knows it                                                                                       |
| `--source <source>`    |          | `auto`  | How a root is mounted, which for an installation is the default. Possible values: `auto`, `directory`, `volumes`, `installation`, `containing-installation`. |
| `-s, --silent`         |          |         | Turn off logging                                                                                                                                             |
| `-v, --verbose`        |          |         | Turn on verbose logging                                                                                                                                      |
| `--json`               |          |         | Write the run's JSON report to stdout, moving human output to stderr                                                                                         |
| `--report <PATH>`      |          |         | Write the run's JSON report to a file                                                                                                                        |
